waiver_targets.name: Germie Bernard
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note:
This article usually doesn't include players who are rostered in 50% or more of Yahoo leagues, but we're making an exception for Germie Bernard, who's rostered in exactly 50% of Yahoo leagues.

If Bernard is unrostered in one of your leagues, there's a good chance it's a shallow league with 10 or fewer teams or extremely short benches. Even if it's that type of a league, Bernard should be rostered.

Injuries to WRs Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson have thrust Bernard into a substantial role, and the second-round rookie appears ready for it. In the Steelers' 26-19 victory over the Buccaneers on Sunday, Bernard had 11-87-1 on 12 targets. He had a 27.3% target share in that contest.

The second-round rookie is going to be ranked inside the top 25 at receiver this week. If Bernard remains unrostered in your league, fix that.

waiver_targets.name: Omar Cooper Jr.
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note:
In his first NFL game, Omar Cooper Jr. played just five offensive snaps and had a 30-yard catch on his only target before sustaining a high-ankle sprain that landed him on IR.

Cooper came off IR in Week 6 and had 6-103-1 on seven targets. His touchdown came on a 48-yard bomb. Cooper also had another touchdown negated by a dubious offensive pass interference penalty called against Jets WR Tim Patrick.

The 30th overall pick in this year's draft, Cooper is a hard-nosed gamer who has good hands and is dangerous after the catch. He can also line up either outside or inside. (Cooper played in the slot on Sunday when the Jets used three-receiver sets.)

Cooper probably isn't going to challenge Garrett Wilson's alpha receiver status on the Jets anytime soon, but he can be an effective No. 2 or No. 3.

Although the Jets will probably be getting Adonai Mitchell back from a finger injury in a week or two, Cooper could be a solution for WR-needy fantasy teams. He has playable matchups against the Dolphins and Raiders the next two weeks.

waiver_targets.name: Jordyn Tyson
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note:
Jordyn Tyson has been on IR with a hamstring injury and could be back as early as this week. The more likely scenario is that he returns in Week 9, after the Saints' Week 8 bye.

Tyson was the eighth overall pick in this year's draft, and some draft analysts believe he's the most talented receiver in the rookie class. Tyson had a strong training camp before injuring his hamstring in a joint practice with the Jaguars. Durability was the biggest knock on Tyson coming out of college, since he had missed games with a variety of ailments.

The Saints have a high-volume passing game, and if Tyson can stay healthy, he could shine alongside star WR Chris Olave.

Tyson will only get more expensive once he's back. This might be your last chance to get him at a reasonable price.

waiver_targets.name: Jakobi Meyers
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note:
Jakobi Meyers is now being rostered in under half of Yahoo leagues, and he probably won't be a popular waiver claim this week with the Jaguars on bye following their two-week residency in London.

A dependable eighth-year veteran, Meyers has 20-285-2 this season on 28 targets. Meyers had 5-83-0 on 10 targets against the Texans in Week 6, with season highs in targets and receiving yardage.

Parker Washington has become the Jaguars' clear No. 1 receiver, but Meyers is No. 2 ahead of the disappointing Brian Thomas. That's not a bad role when your quarterback is Trevor Lawrence and your playcaller is Liam Coen.

Meyers could be a useful depth piece if you don't mind adding a receiver who isn't playing this week.

waiver_targets.name: Jonah Coleman
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note:
Heading into Week 3, Jonah Coleman was a hot waiver pickup because it seemed as if J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey might both miss their next game with hamstring injuries, leaving Coleman with a lead-back role. It turned out Coleman had a high-ankle sprain that led to a stint on injured reserve (IR), while Dobbins and Harvey both played in Week 3.

Fantasy football can be a mischievous imp.

Coleman is eligible to come off IR this week and is expected to suit up for the Broncos' Week 7 game against the Cardinals. He won't command the sort of hefty FAAB bids he drew in Week 3, but Coleman is still worth your attention.

The Broncos' offense is stuck in the mud. Denver has averaged 196 yards of offense over its last two games and has exceeded 300 yards of offense in a game only once this season. QB Bo Nix bears a large share of the blame, but Dobbins is averaging 3.3 yards per carry, while Harvey is averaging 3.9.

The Denver offense could use a spark, and perhaps Coleman could provide it. The rookie from Washington had a strong training camp and looked good in Week 2, when he had 10-39-1 rushing and 3-19-0 receiving against the Jaguars, who have the NFL's best run defense by virtually any statistical measure. Perhaps it's no coincidence that the Broncos rolled up a season-high 392 yards of offense against the Jags that week with Coleman prominently involved.

Although he has the straight-line speed of a tight end, the 5-8, 220-pound Coleman is hard to tackle, has good rushing instincts, is an able pass catcher, and is regarded as a good pass blocker.

Coleman has been out of sight, out of mind during his stay on IR. This is a good chance to acquire a talented young RB who has a chance to have an impactful role for a team in desperate need of an offensive catalyst.

waiver_targets.name: Mike Washington Jr.
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note: Ashton Jeanty has been banged up all season. If Jeanty were to miss any time, rookie Mike Washington Jr. would assume a big workload for Las Vegas. A fourth-round pick out of Arkansas, the 6-1, 223-pound Washington is a size-speed freak who clocked a 4.33 at the scouting combine.

waiver_targets.name: Brian Robinson Jr.
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note: Week 6 was a good reminder that Brian Robinson Jr.'s stand-alone value is fragile. After averaging 10.2 carries over his first five games, Robinson had just two carries for one yard Sunday against the Bears. Atlanta fell into a deep hole against Chicago, and a negative game script is not Robinson's friend. But Robinson remains one of the top handcuff RBs in fantasy football as an insurance policy for Bijan Robinson investors.

waiver_targets.name: Emmett Johnson
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note: Chiefs rookie Emmett Johnson is a dual run-catch threat who would inherit a big workload in a top offense if anything happened to Kenneth Walker III. Johnson is rostered in only 23% of Yahoo leagues.

waiver_targets.name: Samaje Perine
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note: Samaje Perine is unlikely to take Chase Brown's starting job in Cincinnati, but it was eye-opening when Perine out-carried Brown 14-13 in the Bengals' Week 5 win over the Dolphins. Perine was also more effective with his carries in that game, averaging 4.9 yards per carry, while Brown averaged 3.0. Perine is one of the more essential handcuff RBs, and we can't completely discount the possibility that he turns the Bengals' backfield into a timeshare.

waiver_targets.name: Roschon Johnson
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note:
With Kyle Monangai sidelined by turf toe for a second straight week, Roschon Johnson once again backed up starting RB D'Andre Swift in Week 6 and had 13-51-1 rushing and 2-34-0 receiving on two targets against the Falcons.

Monangai could miss another week or two. It would be a stretch to project Johnson for another 15 touches against the Patriots in Week 7. The Bears ran 77 offensive plays and held the ball for just over 40 minutes of clock time in their Week 6 win over the Falcons, which pumped up Johnson's workload.

Still, the Bears have one of the better rushing attacks in the league, and Johnson might be flex-worthy in deeper leagues this week with four teams on bye.

waiver_targets.name: Jaylen Wright
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note: Ollie Gordon has seized command of Miami's lead-back role, but we shouldn't completely dismiss the possibility that Jaylen Wright plays a fantasy-relevant role at some point. Last season, it was often hard to discern whether Gordon or Wright was the top backup to De'Von Achane. It's clear that Gordon is ahead of Wright on the depth chart now, but it's worth keeping the speedy Wright on the radar and perhaps claiming him if you have a roster spot to spare.
